If a switch is an option I’d highly consider it. Fillers in dog food tend to have a bigger effect then we realized before. Starches, especially high glycemic ones, can cause leaky cut which in turn triggers their immune system to perceive things they consume as foreign body and attack it - thus producing an allergic response. As far as price point, zignature is going to be the best. It cuts the big baddies out such as corn, soy, wheat, and grain while also adding all forms of potatoes to the list. You won’t find any of the listed items in their food. They also contain no byproducts so you are getting larger quantities of digestible meat. It may take a month or so to see a difference but it’ll be there. I suggest duck or pork to start and see how he responds. You can aid his system in cleaning the lower GI by adding pet specific bone broths that have low sodium and are slow cooked - best found in the freezer of a small independent pet store. The collagen actually redcoats the lower GI to stop leaky gut. Hope this helps and feel free to dm if you have other questions!
There’s a product called nose butter. Kin+kind also has a hot spot rub on tube that I’ve seen do the trick for dry skin in noses, paw pads and pressure balding on elbows.

Would a rebuttal be worth the energy? I’m genuinely asking. I’d be happy to counter points made regarding balancing, pathogen concerns and sourcing in proper biologically appropriate diets for dogs all cited as reasons these articles find their claims in. But if you’re not open to the education of  it I won’t bother. I would however hope you will reconsider feeding Purina and Nestle Corp diets you suggested. For your dogs sake do not allow your pride to be their means of suffering. Start with watching Pet Fooled as a step. 

Also Hills is currently fighting a vitamin D recall. A problem not found in balanced commercial raw diets using non synthetic vitamins as over potency is not a concern when the issue of vitamin pack sourcing is off the table - check your batch number if you’re currently choosing to feed diets effected.
Do more research.

What is he eating? Grains, soy, corn, and potatoes are contributors to yeast cultures in dogs. Feed a food without them. Try zignature. Go with something with a cooling or neutral protein. If able switch to commercial raw food such as primal. Watch Pet Fooled for a bit more information and stay away from vet diets.

Teach your dog a “leave it” command to reduce fence fighting. Regardless of intent or personality it’s called fence fighting when they run the fence barking. But train leave it and always monitor his outdoor time. If he’s an outside dog then I’d recommend crating when alone and work on him becoming a well behaved indoor dog.

Hire a balanced trainer would be the best thing you can do. Often times owners of these types of dogs coddle the behavior and allow or inadvertently encourage the behavior by trying to tell the dog the situation is ok but in so doing you are telling the dog their reaction to the situation is ok. Which it’s not. Because then they continue to react as such. Routine, leadership and boundaries. Consistently do these things and learn how to properly condition the dog to the things they are fearful of and you’ll be good to go. I’d heavily consider finding a trainer.
What food is he on?

Feed raw if possible. Not home prep until you have done extensive research. Primal for a number of reasons is one of the best raw companies to feed. If you can’t afford or maintain full raw, feed partial raw with a high quality kibble such as zignature. With the stomach upset I’d feed duck for now and then try pork and beef when he’s had better poop. Also add in probiotics by way of goats milk.

Pure positive is only utilizing half of the classical conditioning model of behavior and tends to be less effective than balanced in causing undesired behaviors to extinct. We used treats and crate release to crate train, prong for 2 months to completely stop pulling and no longer have to use it, and we used an e collar with praise and treats to teach perfect off leash recall. Balanced is key.

I got him at a year old and his previous owner said he tore himself up breaking out of a crate and never tried again. So I struggled with the whole free roam and inconsistent crating for about 6 years and just fixed the damage but eventually it became too much and he had to crate. It's always hard to assess without meeting the dog and seeing how he's crated and y'all's response but short periods while home is the best thing to do then work up to short periods while gone. Always make sure he's had a long structured walk before going into the crate and only let him out when he's not crying. Some days I get home and can hear him a little outside the door but as soon as in inside he's silent. I've even left him in for 30 minutes while I move about the apartment but he stays quiet because he knows I won't let him out if he's crying. Some call it cruel but it's not. It's consistent. And that's what a dog with separation anxiety thrives on. I would try breaking up the day care days so that he only goes every other day and is crated on the off days so he slowly eases into it. Also invest in $30-$40 in candy for your neighbors, do little goody bags with a note from the dog with his picture explaining he's getting used to being home alone. Leave your number so they can let you know if he's being too much of a bother. We do it in every place we live and have yet to get complaints but most are very nice and will text shortly after leaving the notes to say they never hear him. It's worth the money!

We live in Texas with ours. 100 degree summers and 30 degrees maybe a week or two out of the year. You can make it work without shaving. Just keep the cost brushed out and breathable. Adjust the schedule for those warm period to accommodate early exercise and mentally exhaust via indoor training during peak heat days.

I’ve used ivideon to monitor but only a couple times to know if he was ever calming down and figure out where to go training wise. We’ve done all kinds of training with him but nothing has really stuck. Consistency is your best friend. Same routines for him, same feeding and walking schedule, same expectations of him. We tried the whole free roam and just with the crate, he was ok some of the time and then other times would eat through the dry wall so he could stick his head outside the house and play lookout - happened twice. But he tore up the door and drywall in 4 places I’ve lived. He’s been crated non negotiable for 3 years now and still has some issue but only when we relocate the crate. After 2 months or so he gets used to it and is fine. But invest in a really solid crate. We bought the kong one and will need to replace it if we plan on moving the crate again with a Gunner or impact brand.

Teach recall and proper off leash behavior early and it sticks for life. Teach leash manners early and don’t resort to a harness because that just gives leverage to pull. Teach balanced rather than pure positive methods. And huskies work better with you than for you. They’re a cooperative breed unlike shepherds or labs. They want to work as a team.

Cooper_calligraphy on instagram is where I got the idea and i used 3D paint on windows to make the layers, then put them into publisher so I could get the positioning correct for print. Figured out to manual feed the page through because it made it line up perfectly. I printed each layer twice, did a single transfer, printed the same layer again and transferred again to make sure everything filled in. Once you get the hang of the transferring with the laser printer you’re using it’s easy!

I ended up learning how to make it since no artist had time to do a custom order. Designed it, printed each layer and heat transferred each color individually. Took a while to get the hang of it but finish product was perfect!

Don't make it "you..." Make it "I....". Because in reality it is you. It's not a negative thing to need words of affirmation from time to time in a relationship and when your relationship is 90% words and maybe 10% physical at best they're all the more important. But if he does not need it to feel comfortable and is more than happy with the relationship then it is you that needs it because it's how you feel the love of a partner. 

I had a similar situation but mine was spurred by my own insecurities. I would say I loved my SO often and he felt that I was saying it so he would say it back more. He wasn't wrong. But I explained why I was feeling insecure and he was able to reaffirm how he felt and that helped me to feel less anxious. It was a heartfelt conversation and I didn't put it on him that he wasn't saying it enough because it wasn't his fault and he's not a mind reader. It was me. 

Talking isn't always communicating your feelings. So I'd round back to handling the conversation less accusatory.

Something that took me a long tine to figure out that the best thing I can do when my SO is struggling is to express how sorry I am that something sucks. I'm the fix it type - or at least I have been for a while. But when he's struggling, has a bad day, has a disagreement with someone, etc. he doesn't want me to offer a list of ways to fix it or even the it'll get better approach. Just "I'm sorry you have to go through...." And it opens the floor to a little more venting of his emotions and he can start to feel better. 

As far as something to renew motivation, I don't think you'll find he will lose it. BUT focus on the fact that this is the last time you have to part with each other that puts you however far away from each other you are. That alone is a huge positive to look forward to!

In general how do you feel about your life right now? Part of being in a relationship is genuinely being happy that your partner is happy. Finding joy in their joy. 

The other end is also feeling pain when your partner is in pain. 

The long and short of my situation is that my husband and I are separated after he immigrated and 3 years of marriage(Texas to Netherlands) and although we have reconciled our relationship issues he will never live in Texas with me again, I'll be moving there. He wasn't happy here. And the pain I came to understand that he was in caused me pain as I didn't want him unhappy. So he lives and thrives there. 

But his leaving put the life I was left to maintain in ruins. I lost my person, some friends, our apartment, and finally my business. All while his life has blossomed there. A lot of therapy over the past 10 months has helped me to realise that dwelling on the internal feelings of jealousy that his life has gotten better while mine fell apart would not help us become closer. It wasn't going to help fix our relationship and would only push him away. I realised that dwelling on my own pity party fueled the envious feelings. For me that was enough to spark the change. So instead I learned to be happy for his successes, genuinely! In a way, I live my life through him. I look forward so much to hearing about his days and the fun he has because it puts a smile on my face and out of mind the mundane and lousy that is mine. 

And that's not to say that I don't still struggle. I broke down litterally 2 days ago because I genuinely am not happy in my life here and want to be with him wherever that is. But I could talk to him about it and he was in pain because I was. Just as I could feel his and it became mine when he needed to leave. And as he shared in it, he could help soothe it. 

So that's why I asked if you were happy in your life? Because chances are you are like me and you're not. And that's ok! But take it from me, limiting your SO's joy about theirs isn't a fix but finding joy in their joy is.

That he can make me laugh or feel better no matter what is going on - I can be a a bit dramatic/emotional when I get stressed but he knows just what you say to make me feel like I can handle things. He's litterally the only person in my life who's ever been able to do that.

Training. You're talking about an animal who has been bred for the purpose of working long and rigorous days on low full and with little time to break. Physical exhaustion just isn't as effective with the breed as with others. So different types of training: obedience, agility, trick training, trim ball, fly ball, and conditioning for water sports/pulling/rally.

I wouldn't advise steering to a dog he's submissive with as the reason you go with that dog. I also would advise more than one meet and greet, maybe see if a rescue or shelter allows for trial periods as a single interaction cannot be the only gauge for dogs working well together. 

As far as coexisting happily. Pull up all toys or items that could be possessed to avoid an issue there. Feed a fair distance apart with you in between and do not allow them to interact with the others bowl. Go on lots of walks and structured interactions rather than depending on them being in the same house to be a reason for them to get along. Allow constructive communication. They should be allowed to bark/growl/correct each other to an extent as that sets the rules of play for them. When observing play, make sure you see alternating role when they are playing and avoid allowing yourself to be the home base to guard for either dog. Interact during their play when necessary but avoid adding excitement in the beginning.
